subject: GPU fleet sufficiency sanity check for late-stage Apogee AI deal
messages:
From: rohan_mehta <rohan@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU fleet sufficiency sanity check for Apogee AI (late-stage)

Team —

Quick one: Apogee AI (APG-2029-347) is pushing toward final procurement next week. They verbally committed to a Dedicated pool size that maps to ~48 A100-equivalent devices for steady-state (in our config that's a mix of reserved V100/4090/Q4 variants). Before we greenlight any formal soft-hold, I need a fast sanity check on current available capacity and realistic ramp windows.

Specifically: 
- What does our usable pool look like for May->Aug (per-week availability broken into zones)?
- Any planned maintenance or capacity reclamation that could materially impact an activation in May?
- Can we put a conditional soft-hold for up to 8 weeks with ops (no billing) and what internal approvals are needed?

Ben — can you pull last 30/60/90-day utilization and a current node map? Marissa — can you estimate the SLA delta if we reserve a 48-device slice vs. 32-device slice (latency/throughput impact)? Connor — please flag any network/placement constraints for east-coast customers.

I attached the quick inventory template (fleet_inventory_Q1.csv) — fill and return by EOD so I can loop in Apogee procurement.

Thanks,
Rohan

Rohan Mehta
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
rohan@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: rohan_mehta <rohan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Apr 2029 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU fleet sufficiency sanity check for Apogee AI (late-stage)

Rohan —

Attached is the populated inventory snapshot (fleet_inventory_Q1.csv) and a quick node-availability heatmap. High-level:
- Week of May 6: nominally ~62 A100-equivalent free units across zones (after committed Reserved pools).
- June: expected drop to ~44 during a scheduled patch window (June 10-14) unless we stagger maintenance.
- July->Aug: capacity recovers to ~58 once a pending customer migration finishes (ETA Jul 22).

Notes / caveats:
- The A100-equivalent calculation includes a mix of 80% A100 / 10% 4090 / 10% Q4 margins; if Apogee insists on strict A100 certification we should subtract ~10% for compatibility testing.
- We can do an 8-week conditional soft-hold. Ops requires formal approval from Capacity (SLA exceptions) + an internal billing note. Operationally that hold would mark the nodes as "reserved-contingent" (no consumer billing) and prevent autoscale from pulling them for spot-like workloads.

I'll flag the June patch with infra and ask if it can be windowed. If Ops is confident we can stagger, the May activation looks safe.

Attachments: fleet_inventory_Q1.csv (attachment stub), node_heatmap_may_aug.png (attachment stub)

—Ben
Ben Carter
Capacity Planning Lead
ben@redwood.com

From: Alicia Ramos <alicia@apogee.ai>
To: rohan_mehta <rohan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@apogee.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU fleet sufficiency sanity check for Apogee AI (late-stage)

Hi Rohan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We need to finalize sizing this week for our board packet. A few points from our side: 
- Target steady throughput estimate: ~1100 tokens/s for embeddings pipelines + 420 tokens/s for interactive inference (our infra team modeled this to your A100-equivalent translation).
- Preferred start date: May 10 (with a 2-week validation/canary).
- We are open to a phased reservation: 32 devices initially, scale to 48 after validation.

Please confirm whether the conditional soft-hold is possible without an upfront commitment. Also, can you share any specific acceptance tests you'd expect during the 2-week validation (we prefer a short runbook so our SREs can parallel your checks).

Attached: draft MOU (apogee_mou_draft.pdf)

Best,
Alicia Ramos
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Apogee AI
Alicia.Ramos@apogee.ai

From: rohan_mehta <rohan@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@apogee.ai>, procurement@apogee.ai
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU fleet sufficiency sanity check for Apogee AI (late-stage)

Alicia / procurement —

Appreciate the clarity and the draft MOU. Good news: Ben's inventory shows we can support your phased plan starting May 10 provided we get ops assurance on the June patch window (we're already asking infra to shorten/distribute it).

Next steps from Redwood: 
- Ops: I am requesting a conditional soft-hold for 32 devices starting May 6 (no billing until activation; hold valid up to 8 weeks). Please acknowledge if Capacity can apply the hold and list any gating approvals. (Ben/Connor/Marissa, please coordinate offline and mark the nodes as reserved-contingent once approved).
- SRE/Validation: we'll provide a short acceptance runbook (3 tests) within 24 hours — quick perf baseline, KV-cache warm test, and multi-session stability under 75% load. I will attach the runbook once it's finalized.
- Legal/Procurement: Rohan will push a short MOU for signature that documents the phased start + conditional hold terms.

If we get Ops acknowledgement by EOD today, I'll confirm May 10 as a target start with your procurement team.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Rohan
